transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, yeah, nice to meet you too. Um, I guess I came in because... well, I'm a high school teacher. And I'll sit down with a stack of essays or like, a new curriculum document, fully intending to just power through and work. 

Like, this past weekend I had this huge pile of papers on the Industrial Revolution. Which, honestly, the kids actually did a pretty good job on this year. Usually it's like pulling teeth to get 10th graders to care about the spinning jenny or textile mills, you know? One kid even made this little 3D model out of popsicle sticks for extra credit, which was wild because he usually never turns in his regular homework, so I was actually pretty impressed... 

But, um, anyway, sorry. What was I saying? Right, the grading. I'll sit down to grade them, and within ten minutes I'll realize I’ve just been staring at the exact same page the whole time. Like, my eyes are on the paper, but I'm thinking about three completely different things—like if I need to get my car's oil changed, or a podcast I listened to yesterday—and I'm barely taking in a single word of what's actually in front of me.
Did you have this kind of trouble focusing when you were a child?

Yeah, actually, I did. I mean, even way back in primary school. I remember my parents used to get so frustrated with me. My mom had this whole filing system for my brother's schoolwork, like these color-coded binders, which is funny because my brother is an accountant now, so I guess the organization really rubbed off on him. He lives in Chicago, actually, just bought a place out there near the lake. 

But anyway, my stuff? Not organized at all. My parents were constantly finding old worksheets just completely crumpled up at the bottom of my backpack. Like, I would actually do the homework sometimes and then just totally forget to turn it in. I had this blue JanSport bag that was basically a black hole for paper. And my report cards always said the exact same thing every single year. The teachers would write that I was bright but careless, or they would complain that I wouldn't finish my work unless I was being closely supervised by them. So yeah, it definitely goes pretty far back.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days lately?

No, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I feel down. Mostly I just feel... frustrated? Like, annoyed with myself for not getting things done. But not sad. Honestly, the weather's been so nice lately, it's hard to be too bummed out. I actually went for a hike this past weekend up at State Park. The leaves are just starting to change, which is my absolute favorite time of year. I usually try to get up there at least twice in October. My buddy Dave was supposed to come with me, but his dog had this weird stomach thing, so he had to stay home. It's a Golden Retriever, super cute, but man, that dog eats everything. He ate an entire sock once. 

But yeah, anyway, no, I don't think I'm depressed. Just... scattered, I guess.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying, even when there isn’t an obvious reason to?

No, I wouldn't say I'm a big worrier. I mean, I stress about the grading piling up, but that's a pretty obvious reason, right? It's not like I'm just sitting around anxious about nothing. Actually, my mom is the worrier in the family. She watches the news constantly, like, 24/7. I keep telling her she needs to turn off the TV and maybe read a book or something, but she says she likes to stay informed. She called me the other day panicking because she heard about some new scam going around where people steal your information through text messages. I had to spend like twenty minutes explaining to her how two-factor authentication works. Which, honestly, is such a pain to set up, but I guess it's worth it. I had to redo all my passwords last month because I got locked out of my school email... but yeah, no, I don't really worry about stuff for no reason. Just the normal stuff.
